Rashi on Ketubot 48a:11:1.english: One who says - At the time of his death.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:11:2.hebrew: אם מתה אשתו כו' שומעין לו - דכיון דהוא מת בחייה והיא גובה כתובתה, אינו חייב לקוברה, דתנן (לקמן כתובות דף צה:): יורשיה יורשי כתובתה חייבין בקבורתה:
Rashi on Ketubot 48a:11:2.english: If his wife dies, etc., we listen to him - For since he died during her lifetime and she collects her ketubah, he is not obligated to bury her, as we learned in a Mishnah (below, Ketubot 95b): "Her heirs, the heirs of her ketubah, are obligated in her burial."

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:11:3.english: The property is cast before the orphans - And it is obvious that her burial is not [incumbent] upon them.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:12:1.english: Do not bury him from his property - but rather from charity.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:13:1.hebrew: לעולם היא ברשות האב - ואם בת ישראל מאורסה לכהן היא, אינה אוכלת בתרומה, וזכאי בה ככל זכות אב בבתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 48a:13:1.english: She is always under the father's authority - And if she is the daughter of an Israelite betrothed to a priest, she may not eat terumah, and he [the father] is entitled to every right of a father over his daughter.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:1:1.hebrew: לפום שארה - זקינה, קשה לה משאוי ואינה יכולה לסבול בגדים רחבים, וילדה צריכה בגדים רחבים להתנאות בהם:
Rashi on Ketubot 48a:1:1.english: In accordance with her flesh - [For] an elderly woman, weight is hard for her and she cannot bear wide garments, whereas a young girl needs wide garments to adorn herself with them.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:1:2.hebrew: לפום עונתה - לפי העת, אם חמה אם צנה:
Rashi on Ketubot 48a:1:2.english: In accordance with her time [of year] - According to the season, whether [it is] heat or cold.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:1:3.english: New [garments] - They are warmer than worn-out [garments].

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:3:1.english: That it is her custom - The practice of the women of her family is thus.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:3:2.english: What is the reason of the first Tanna - Who says [he] does not need [to].

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:4:1.english: His custom - For the daughters of his family they do so.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:4:2.hebrew: עולה עמו ואינה יורדת עמו - מבעולת בעל נפקא לן, בעלייתו של בעל ולא בירידתו של בעל, בפרק אע"פ (שם.):
Rashi on Ketubot 48a:4:2.english: [She] ascends with him and does not descend with him - We derive [this] from [the phrase] "married to a husband" — [she shares] in the ascent of the husband and not in the descent of the husband — in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (ibid.).

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:4:3.hebrew: ה"מ מחיים - כגון: הוא אומר להניק את בנה, והיא אומרת שלא להניק, ודרך בנות משפחתה להניק בניהם ולא דרך משפחתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 48a:4:3.english: This applies only [when they are] alive - For example: he says [for her] to nurse her son and she says not to nurse [him], and [it is] the custom of the daughters of her family to nurse their sons, but not the custom of his family.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:6:2.english: Provide a livelihood - [This refers to] clothing and garments.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:6:3.english: And something else - [The Gemara] explains [this] below.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:6:4.english: But not his sons and daughters - For he is not obligated in their sustenance during his lifetime.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:7:1.hebrew: ולא שאני לך כו' - יוצא מן המקום לדעת, היה בידו לצוות על מזונות בניו ובנותיו ואשתו, ולא צוה, גילה דעתו שאינו רוצה לזונן. הילכך, אשתו דמיחייב לה בתנאי כתובה, אשתעבוד ניכסיה; בניו ובנותיו, לא. אבל נשתטה, דיצא מן העולם שלא לדעת, מסתמא ניחא ליה שיזונו בניו ובנותיו משלו:
Rashi on Ketubot 48a:7:1.english: And is there no difference for you, etc. - [One who] departs from the place knowingly had it in his power to give instructions regarding the sustenance of his sons, his daughters, and his wife, and did not give instructions — he revealed his intention that he does not wish to sustain them. Therefore, [as for] his wife, to whom he is obligated by the stipulation of the ketubah, his property is encumbered; [as for] his sons and daughters, [it is] not. However, [if] he became insane, for he departed from the world [of reason] unknowingly, presumably it is pleasing to him that his sons and daughters be sustained from his [property].

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:8:1.english: Ornaments - Perfumes of merchant's powder with which women adorn themselves.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:8:2.hebrew: מ"ד תכשיט - לא יהבינן לאשתו, כ"ש שאין עלינו לעשות צדקה מנכסיו. ואמתניתא קיימי:
Rashi on Ketubot 48a:8:2.english: The one who says ornaments - [meaning] we do not give [ornaments] to his wife; all the more so that it is not incumbent upon us to give charity from his property. And they are referring to the baraita.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:8:3.hebrew: לא ניחא ליה דתינוול - אע"פ שלא צוה בלכתו, עבדינן. ולא נראה, דאדמר עוקבא קיימי דאמר מי שנשתטה יורדין לנכסיו וזנין כו' וד"א, ואיפכא גרסינן: מ"ד צדקה — כ"ש תכשיט, ומ"ד תכשיט — אבל צדקה לא; התם היינו טעמא, דלא ניחא ליה דתינוול:
Rashi on Ketubot 48a:8:3.english: It is not satisfactory for him that she be demeaned - Even though he did not command [this] when he departed, we do [it]. However, [this explanation] does not seem [correct], for they are referring to [the statement of] Mar Ukva, who said: "One who became insane, we go down to his property and sustain [his wife and children] etc. and [give] something else." And we read the reverse: "The one who says charity — all the more so ornaments; and the one who says ornaments — but charity [we do] not [give]." There, that is the reason: that it is not satisfactory for him that she be demeaned.

Rashi on Ketubot 48a:9:1.hebrew: לפי כבודו ולא לפי כבודה - בתמיה. מידי דאורחה ולאו אורחיה, מי לא בעי למיעבד לה? הא ודאי אינה יורדת עמו, ואפילו למאן דלית ליה עולה עמו לאחר מיתה, אינה יורדת אית ליה:
Rashi on Ketubot 48a:9:1.english: In accordance with his dignity and not in accordance with her dignity - [This is asked] in astonishment: something that is her custom and not his custom, does he not have to do [it] for her? Surely she does not descend with him! And even according to the one who does not hold [that] "she ascends with him" [applies] after death, he does hold [that] "she does not descend."

Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:13:1.hebrew: לעולם היא ברשות האב עד שתכנס לחופה גרסינן - ול"ג "עד שתכנס לרשות הבעל", דא"כ הוה משמע עד שימסור האב לשלוחי הבעל, כדמוכח בגמרא, דקאמר רב נחמן בר יצחק: אף אנן נמי תנינא "הבא על אשת איש כו'" — לרשות הבעל בעלמא. ומתני' דהכא מוקמינן לה בגמרא לענין תרומה, לאפוקי ממשנה ראשונה; א"כ הויא תיובתא דרב, דאמר בגמרא: מסירתה לכל חוץ מלתרומה. ומיהו י"ל: דהא דדייק רב נחמן בר יצחק בגמרא היינו מדקתני "כיון שנכנסה כו'", לכך משמע ליה אפילו מסר; אבל הכא, דקתני "לעולם היא ברשות האב עד שתכנס לרשות הבעל", משמע שפיר דהיינו עד שתכנס לחופה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:13:1.english: "She is always under her father’s authority until she enters the bridal canopy [chuppah]" — this is the text we read - And we do not read "until she enters the husband’s authority," for if so, it would imply until the father delivers [her] to the husband’s agents, as is proven in the Gemara, where Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak says: "We have also learned: One who cohabits with a married woman, etc." — [referring to] the husband’s authority in general [i.e., even via delivery to agents]. And our Mishnah here we establish in the Gemara as referring to terumah, to exclude the earlier Mishnah; if so, it would be a refutation of Rav, who says in the Gemara: Her delivery [to the husband’s agents] is effective for everything except terumah. However, one can say that what Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak infers in the Gemara is from the fact that it teaches "Once she has entered, etc.," therefore it implies to him even if [the father] delivered [her]; whereas here, where it teaches "She is always under her father’s authority until she enters the husband’s authority," it properly implies that this means until she enters the bridal canopy.

Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:1:1.hebrew: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב אומר שארה כסותה לפום שארה תן כסותה כו' - פירש רשב"ם דרבי אליעזר בן יעקב סבר נמי דמזונות דאורייתא, דהכי מתניא סיפא דברייתא: "מזונות מנין? אמרת ק"ו: ומה דברים שאין בהן קיום נפש כך, דברים שיש בהן קיום נפש — על אחת כמה וכמה. דרך ארץ מנין? אמרת קל וחומר: ומה דברים שלא נישאת עליהם לכתחילה אינו רשאי למנוע ממנה, דברים שנישאת עליהם לכתחילה — אינו דין שאינו רשאי למנוע ממנה?" ולפי זה תימה: ברייתא דלעיל, דקתני "תיקנו מזונות תחת מעשה ידיה", דמשמע דמזונות דרבנן — כמאן אתיא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:1:1.english: "Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says: She'era kesuta — in accordance with her flesh [she'era], give her clothing [kesuta], etc." - Rashbam explained that Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov also holds that sustenance [is] by Torah law, for thus the latter part of the baraita teaches: "From where [do we derive] sustenance? You say [it is] an a fortiori inference: If [for] things that are not [essential for] the preservation of life [it is] so, [then for] things that are [essential for] the preservation of life — how much more so! From where [do we derive] marital relations [derekh eretz]? You say [it is] an a fortiori inference: If [for] things for which she was not initially married he is not permitted to withhold from her, [then for] things for which she was initially married — is it not logical that he is not permitted to withhold [them] from her?" And according to this, [it is] puzzling: the baraita above, which teaches: "They instituted sustenance in exchange for her handiwork," which implies that sustenance [is] by rabbinic law — in accordance with whom does it follow?

Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:4:1.hebrew: דאורחיה דידיה ולאו אורחה דידה - פי' בקונטרס: דאורחיה בבנות משפחתו, אבל אין דרך בבנות משפחתה. וקשה: דאמאי נקט "שני חלילין ומקוננת אחת"? הוה ליה למינקט "לא יפחות לה מדרכו". ואומר רבינו תם: דאורחיה דידיה היינו אפי' לעני שבישראל אין פוחתין משני חלילין ומקוננת, אבל לנקיבות יש שפוחתין; וקאמר ר' יהודה "לא יפחות משני חלילין", אע"ג דאם לא נישאת שמא היו פוחתין לה, כיון דנישאת — לא יפחות לה, כמו שאין פוחתין לו. ומיהו הלשון דחוק, דקאמר "כגון דאורחיה דידיה", משמע דאיכא דלאו אורחיה בהכי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:4:1.english: Where it is his custom, and not her custom - Rashi [lit. the Kuntres] explained: that it is customary among the women of his family, but it is not the custom among the women of her family. And this is difficult: why did [the Mishnah] specify "two flutes and one wailing woman"? It should have stated, "[her husband] may not give her less than his [family's] custom." And Rabbeinu Tam says: "it is his custom" means [that for males,] even for the poorest man in Israel, they do not provide fewer than two flutes and a wailing woman, whereas for females there are those who provide fewer; and Rabbi Yehudah says, "he may not provide fewer than two flutes" — even though if she had not married they might have provided fewer for her, once she has married, he may not provide fewer for her, just as they do not provide fewer for him. However, the wording is forced, for when [the Gemara] says, "where it is his custom," it implies that there is someone for whom this is not his custom.

Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:7:1.hebrew: ולא שאני לך בין יוצא לדעת ליוצא שלא לדעת - לקמן בפ' בתרא (כתובות דף קז. ושם), דמוקי לה ההיא דמי שהלך למדינת הים כשהשרה אשתו ע"י שליש אבל לא בניו ובנותיו — משמע דקודם שיצא לא היה משרה אותם, אבל אם היה משרה אותם גם אנו היינו זנין אותם, כיון דניחא ליה. ולפי זה צריך לומר ההיא דמי שנשתטה — דזנין בניו ובנותיו אפי' לא היה משרה אותם מתחלה. ואין נראה לר"י, דאם לא השרה אותם מתחלה ע"י שליש ולא פירנסם, אמאי מפרנסין אותם? אלא ודאי איירי כשהיה מפרנסם קודם, וכן ההיא דמי שהלך למדינת הים, מדפריך מינה אההיא דנשתטה. ובפ' בתרא דמוקי לה במשרה אשתו על ידי שליש אבל לא בניו ובנותיו — היינו בשעה שהלך הניח מעות ביד שליש לפרנס אשתו, ולא הניח לפרנס בניו; אבל קודם שהלך, היו כולם ניזונין משלו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:7:1.english: Is there no difference for you between one who leaves knowingly and one who leaves unknowingly? - Later in the last chapter (Ketubot 107a and there), where [the Gemara] establishes that [baraita] of "one who went overseas" as [a case] where he provided for his wife through a third party, but not his sons and daughters — this implies that before he left he was not providing for them, whereas if he had been providing for them, we too would feed them, since he is amenable to it. And according to this, one must say [regarding] that [baraita] of "one who lost his sanity" that we feed his sons and daughters even if he had not been providing for them initially. However, this does not appear [correct] to the Ri, for if he did not provide for them initially through a third party and did not support them, why would we support them? Rather, it certainly refers to [a case] where he was supporting them beforehand — and likewise that [baraita] of "one who went overseas," since [the Gemara] raises an objection from it against that [baraita] of "one who lost his sanity." And in the last chapter, where [the Gemara] establishes it as [a case where] he provides for his wife through a third party, but not his sons and daughters — that means that at the time he left he deposited money in the hand of a third party to support his wife, and did not deposit [money] to support his children; however, before he left, all of them were being fed from his [property].

Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:8:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: "מאי 'ולא דבר אחר'?", וגרסינן נמי: "ומאן דאמר צדקה — אבל תכשיט יהבינן לה, דלא ניחא ליה דתינוול"; דאההיא ד"מי שהלך" איפליגו בה בהדיא בפרק בתרא (לקמן כתובות דף קז.):
Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:8:1.english: This is the proper reading: "What is 'and not something else'?" And we also read: "And [according to] the one who says charity — but we give her ornaments, since it is not satisfactory to him that she be demeaned"; for regarding that [case] of "One who went [overseas]," they explicitly disagreed about it in the last chapter (below, Ketubot 107a).

Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:8:2.hebrew: תכשיט - והא דאמר בפרק המדיר (לקמן כתובות דף עא:): פוסקין קישוטין לאשה — היינו כל זמן שהוא עמה, שלא תתגנה עליו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:8:2.english: Ornaments - And that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Hamadir (below, Ketubot 71b): "[The court] allocates ornaments for a woman" — that is [only] as long as he is with her, so that she will not become repulsive to him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:9:1.hebrew: מי שהלך למדינת הים כו' - אית ספרים דגרסי: קוברין אותה לפי כבודה; לפי כבודה אין, לפי כבודו לא?! אימא אף לפי כבודה. ואין נראה: חדא, דאמאי נקט "מי שהלך למדינת הים"? אדרבה, טפי הוי רבותא דאפי' כשהוא אצלה דאינה יורדת עמו, וכ"ש כשאינו אצלה! ועוד, מאי "אפי' לאחר מיתה" דקאמר? אדרבה, טפי הוי רבותא במחיים מלאחר מיתה! ועוד, דקאמר "אימא אף לפי כבודה" — אדרבה, לפי כבודו הוי רבותא טפי, דלא הוי אלא לר' יהודה; אבל לפי כבודה, דאינה יורדת עמו, לא הוי רבותא כולי האי, דהא לעיל פריך: "אי דאורחה, מ"ט דת"ק?" — משמע דמילתא דפשיטא הוא. ונראה לר"ת דגרסינן: קוברין אותה לפי כבודו; לפי כבודו אין, לפי כבודה לא?! אימא אף לפי כבודו. אבל קשה לרשב"א: דאמאי קמתמה "לפי כבודו ולא לפי כבודה"? אמאי סלקא דעתיה דנקט "לפי כבודו" דוקא ולא לפי כבודה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 48a:9:1.english: "One who went overseas, etc." - There are books that read [the Gemara's text as]: "[They] bury her in accordance with her dignity." [To which the Gemara asks:] "In accordance with her dignity, yes, [and] in accordance with his dignity, no?! Say: even in accordance with her dignity." But this does not appear [correct]. Firstly, why did [the Gemara] state "one who went overseas"? On the contrary, it would be a greater novelty [to say] that even when he is with her, [the rule is] that she does not descend [in dignity] with him, and all the more so when he is not with her! Furthermore, what is [the meaning of] "even after death" that [the Gemara] says [below]? On the contrary, it is a greater novelty [to state this rule] during [her] lifetime than after death! Furthermore, [as to] what it says, "Say: even in accordance with her dignity" — on the contrary, [burying her] in accordance with his dignity is a greater novelty, for it is only according to Rabbi Yehudah; whereas [burying her] in accordance with her dignity, [following the principle] that she does not descend with him, is not such a great novelty, for above [the Gemara] asked: "If it is her custom, what is the reason of the Tanna Kamma?" — which implies that it is an obvious matter. Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that we read: "[They] bury her in accordance with his dignity." [The Gemara asks:] "In accordance with his dignity, yes, [and] in accordance with her dignity, no?!" "Say: also in accordance with his dignity." However, it is difficult for the Rashba: Why does [the Gemara] wonder, "In accordance with his dignity and not in accordance with her dignity"? Why would it enter [the Gemara's] mind that it stated "in accordance with his dignity" specifically, and not in accordance with her dignity?
